seat_rationales.reasoning: Contemporary reporting confirms Heath Robinson died of burn-pit-linked cancer affecting his lungs and body, with a plausible toxicological mechanism; the government 'inadequate evidence' items address unproven population-level association, not the individual presumptive cause, so they do not contradict the core claim.
Core claim asserts direct causation (cancer from burn-pit exposure ravaged Heath); E1/E3 government reviews explicitly found inadequate evidence of any such association as of 2020-2021.
provided evidence does not establish or disprove the specific medical causation that Heath’s cancer was caused by burn-pit exposure

biden_2022:0432.snippet: [2020-09-11] National Academies (2020) concluded evidence was inadequate/insufficient to determine an association between burn pits and respiratory cancers.
[2022-03-01] Local report on SOTU guest Danielle Robinson; details husband Heath's cancer from prolonged burn-pit exposure.
[2021-02-22] VA WRIISC (updated Feb 22, 2021) states research at that time did not show evidence of long‑term health problems from burn pits.
[2022-03-01] USA Today/Yahoo coverage of Biden honoring Heath Robinson, who died of burn-pit-linked cancer affecting lungs/body.
[2021-04-16] EPA summary of simulated burn‑pit smoke testing (SOT 2021) reported PAHs and lung toxicity in animal models, indicating plausible harm to lungs.
[2021-05-27] VA announcement (May 27, 2021) describing review/possible expansion of presumptive conditions related to particulate/burn‑pit exposures.
[2021-02-24] Senate bill text (S.437, Feb 24, 2021) acknowledges veteran health concerns and calls for concession/recognition of burn‑pit exposures.
